facts.text: Prairie Farm was founded in 1848 by the lumber company Knapp, Stout and Company, making it the oldest European settlement in Barron County.
Early pioneers named Prairie Farm after the expansive, fertile grasslands they found throughout the region during the late nineteenth century.
Before European settlement, the Prairie Farm area served as a traditional homeland for the Ojibwe people for hunting and seasonal migration.
The village of Prairie Farm sits on the eastern shore of the Prairie Farm Flowage, a reservoir on the Hay River.
Rail service arrived in 1900 via the Menomonie, Dallas and Rice Lake Railroad, allowing farmers to ship agricultural products to larger markets.
Prairie Farm celebrated its 175th anniversary in 2023, marking its evolution from a nineteenth-century farming outpost into a modern rural community.
